# Results — Study 940 (The Turnover Budget) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One sleeve, four speeds: rank
the eleven **Select Sector SPDRs** on their **12-1** total return (trailing 252 days,
skipping the last 21), go long the top 3 and short the bottom 3, equal-weighted, 0.5 gross
per side — **dollar-neutral, 1.0 gross**. The only thing that changes across arms is the
rebalance clock: **daily / weekly / monthly / quarterly**. Signal formed through day `t`,
weights effective for day `t+1`, trade charged on `t+1` — **one execution lag, and only
one**. Weights **drift** with returns between rebalances and are renormalised by the book's
own return, so gross exposure stays at its mandate. Daily **total-return** closes
(`yfinance`, `auto_adjust=True`). As-of **2026-06-30** (the partial current month is
dropped).*

*A dollar-neutral book is funded by its own collateral, which earns the bill, so the
long-minus-short spread **is** the excess-of-cash return — subtracting BIL again would
double-count. BIL therefore gates only the long-only cross-check (from its 2007 inception),
not the headline.*

## Data stamp

| Legs | Window | n days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| XLB XLC XLE XLF XLI XLK XLP XLRE XLU XLV XLY + BIL | 1999-12-23 → 2026-06-30 | 6,668 | Fingerprint `7af2719e8031` |

`quantlab.repro.fingerprint` over the full cached frame (the eleven sectors + BIL + SPY):
`acd0de4000fe`.

Sector panel begins 1998-12-22 (SPDR inception); the first tradable day is 1999-12-23 once
the 12-1 window fills. **XLRE lists in 2015 and XLC in 2018**, so investable breadth grows
9 → 11; a sector is NaN (not investable) before its own inception rather than back-filled.
SPY is cached as the cap-weight reference.

> **Why the fingerprint is load-bearing.** These are `auto_adjust=True` total-return closes,
> and a total-return series is **re-based over its whole history** every time a new dividend
> lands. Refetching the cache therefore moves numbers in the third decimal even though the
> window and the code are unchanged (an earlier cut of this file, on fingerprint
> `2261d3056761`, had a monthly gross Sharpe of +0.088 against the +0.099 below). Quote the
> fingerprint or the run is not reproducible.

## Non-tape inputs (assumptions, all swept)

| Input | Base | Swept over | Why it is an assumption |
|---|--:|---|---|
| Cost per unit traded notional | 5 bps | 0 / 1 / 2.5 / 5 / 10 / 25 | Spread + impact are not in a daily close tape |
| Borrow on the short leg | 40 bps/yr | 0 / 25 / 50 / 100 | Sector SPDRs are general collateral; the rate is quoted, not observed here |

## The headline — the turnover budget

Cost 5 bps per unit traded notional, borrow 40 bps/yr. **Annual turnover** is traded notional
per year in units of NAV. **Break-even** is the cost per unit traded notional at which that
arm's net excess return is exactly zero (borrow still paid) — the budget itself.

| Speed | Rebalances | Annual turnover | Gross exSharpe (HAC *t*) | Net exSharpe | **Break-even** |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Daily** | 6,668 | **31.3×** | +0.121 (*t* = +0.67) | −0.096 | **2.5 bps** |
| **Weekly** | 1,384 | 13.4× | +0.105 (*t* = +0.59) | −0.003 | **4.8 bps** |
| **Monthly** | 318 | 5.8× | +0.099 (*t* = +0.55) | **+0.037** | **10.1 bps** |
| **Quarterly** | 106 | 3.3× | +0.013 (*t* = +0.07) | −0.034 | **−3.2 bps** |

Gross annualised excess return: +0.98% / +0.85% / +0.79% / +0.10%. Vol is ~8% at every
speed; worst drawdown −36.7% / −31.7% / −26.3% / −39.4%.

- **The budget exists arithmetically and is worthless statistically.** The best gross HAC
  *t* across all four speeds is **+0.67**. There is no gross return to spend, so the
  break-even numbers are estimates of a quantity that is not distinguishable from zero.
- **Speed buys almost nothing gross.** Daily earns +0.98%/yr gross against monthly's
  +0.79% — a Sharpe gap of +0.012 (HAC *t* = +0.18) — and pays **5.4× the turnover** for it.
- **92-93% of the traded notional is rank churn**, not weight drift. Only ~8% of the
  daily arm's trading is snapping still-held names back to equal weight; the rest is the
  signal changing its mind about which sector belongs in the book. A no-trade band would
  therefore save little.

## The cost surface (net excess-of-cash Sharpe, borrow 40 bps)

| Cost/unit turnover | daily | weekly | monthly | quarterly |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross of trading) | **+0.097** | +0.080 | +0.073 | −0.014 |
| 1 bp | +0.058 | +0.063 | **+0.066** | −0.018 |
| 2.5 bps | +0.000 | +0.039 | **+0.055** | −0.024 |
| **5 bps** | −0.096 | −0.003 | **+0.037** | −0.034 |
| 10 bps | −0.288 | −0.086 | **+0.001** | −0.055 |
| 25 bps | −0.862 | −0.334 | **−0.109** | −0.118 |

The frequency ranking **inverts below the first basis point**: daily is the best arm at 0 bps
and already third at 1 bp, and monthly owns every row thereafter. By 2.5 bps daily is last.
An execution standard under 1 bp is not something anyone clears on a book that trades 31×
its NAV a year.

## Borrow sweep (net excess Sharpe, cost 5 bps)

| Borrow | daily | weekly | monthly | quarterly |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps/yr | −0.071 | +0.022 | +0.062 | −0.008 |
| 25 bps/yr | −0.087 | +0.006 | +0.047 | −0.025 |
| 50 bps/yr | −0.102 | −0.009 | +0.031 | −0.041 |
| 100 bps/yr | −0.133 | −0.040 | −0.001 | −0.074 |

Borrow is a *holding* cost, so it moves every speed by roughly the same amount and cannot
rescue or condemn any of them. Even at zero borrow the best arm is +0.062.

## Parameter robustness (gross excess Sharpe, monthly clock)

The sort is fixed at the Jegadeesh-Titman convention (252-day lookback, 21-day skip, top/bottom
3) and was **not** tuned. The neighbourhood is reported so nobody has to take that on trust:

| top_k | lookback | skip | Gross exSharpe | HAC *t* | Gross ann. |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2 | 252 | 21 | +0.055 | +0.31 | +0.56% |
| **3** | **252** | **21** | **+0.099** | **+0.55** | **+0.79%** |
| 4 | 252 | 21 | +0.072 | +0.39 | +0.47% |
| 5 | 252 | 21 | −0.006 | −0.02 | −0.03% |
| 3 | 126 | 21 | +0.020 | +0.11 | +0.16% |
| 3 | 252 | 0 | +0.046 | +0.25 | +0.36% |
| 3 | 63 | 5 | +0.003 | +0.02 | +0.03% |

The headline parametrisation is the *best* of the seven — and its *t* is **+0.55**. There is
no corner of this neighbourhood where the sleeve is significant, which is the point: the
published setting was not cherry-picked, and cherry-picking would not have helped.

| Speed | Gross | 95% CI | Net (5/40) | 95% CI | share < 0 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| daily | +0.121 | [−0.221, +0.473] | −0.096 | [−0.431, +0.252] | 71.2% |
| weekly | +0.105 | [−0.232, +0.457] | −0.003 | [−0.337, +0.348] | 51.4% |
| monthly | +0.099 | [−0.252, +0.449] | +0.037 | [−0.313, +0.388] | 41.4% |
| quarterly | +0.013 | [−0.319, +0.346] | −0.034 | [−0.366, +0.297] | 58.8% |

Every interval straddles zero, gross and net, at every speed.

## Head-to-head speed races (paired, same tape, same signal)

| Race | Gross Sharpe gap (HAC *t*) | Net Sharpe gap (HAC *t*) |
|---|--:|--:|
| daily − monthly | +0.012 (*t* = +0.18) | −0.144 (*t* = −1.90) |
| daily − quarterly | +0.098 (*t* = +0.90) | −0.072 (*t* = −0.67) |
| monthly − quarterly | +0.086 (*t* = +1.02) | +0.071 (*t* = +0.84) |

Not one race clears |*t*| = 2. Even "monthly beats daily net" — the result the whole study
is shaped to detect — is only *t* = −1.90.

## Era cut (split 2013-01-01)

The signal is rebuilt inside each half, so each half spends its first twelve months warming
up the 12-1 window and 2013 sits in neither table. Not a clean partition; named as such.

| Speed | 1999–2012 gross exSharpe | break-even | 2013–2026 gross exSharpe | break-even |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| daily | +0.035 | **+0.3 bps** | +0.154 | **+3.5 bps** |
| weekly | +0.103 | +4.9 bps | +0.047 | +1.2 bps |
| monthly | +0.137 | **+15.9 bps** | +0.014 | **−1.7 bps** |
| quarterly | +0.013 | −3.0 bps | −0.022 | −11.1 bps |

The budget **re-orders completely**. Monthly is the roomiest arm in the first half (15.9 bps)
and *negative* in the second (−1.7 bps); daily is the tightest in the first half and second
roomiest in the last. No half has a gross *t* above +0.56. A budget that swaps its winner
across eras is a noise estimate, not a capacity number.

## Long-only cross-check (top-3 long, excess of BIL, 2007-05-30 → 2026-06-30)

The control is the **same eleven sectors, equal-weighted over the same investable universe,
run through the same engine, on the same rebalance clock, with the same one-day lag, paying
the same 5 bps on its own traded notional.** Cost symmetry is not a nicety: the sleeve turns
over roughly 18-20× more than the control, so a frictionless benchmark hands the sleeve's
entire commission back as fake underperformance.

| Speed | Net exSharpe | HAC *t* vs cash | EW-11 exSharpe | Alpha vs EW (gross) | *t* | Alpha vs EW (net) | *t* | Turnover | EW turnover |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| daily | +0.524 | **+2.56** | +0.556 | **+0.67%/yr** | +0.35 | −0.62%/yr | −0.33 | 27.2× | 1.49× |
| weekly | +0.546 | **+2.65** | +0.555 | +0.40%/yr | +0.21 | −0.19%/yr | −0.10 | 12.4× | 0.72× |
| monthly | +0.539 | **+2.62** | +0.551 | +0.09%/yr | +0.05 | −0.15%/yr | −0.08 | 5.2× | 0.37× |
| quarterly | +0.535 | **+2.62** | +0.584 | −0.31%/yr | −0.17 | −0.44%/yr | −0.24 | 2.8× | 0.24× |

This is the trap the study exists to name. Every long-only arm clears *t* = 2 against cash —
because a book that is 100% in equities at all times is being measured against T-bills. Against
the no-view control the selection alpha is **±0.7%/yr with every |*t*| ≤ 0.35**: nothing, at
any speed. The significance is equity beta wearing a momentum label.

> **Audit correction.** The first cut of this table raced the *costed* momentum sleeve against
> a **frictionless**, daily-rebalanced equal-weight average, and reported selection alpha of
> −0.42% to −0.94%/yr — "momentum loses to equal weighting at every speed". That gap was, to
> the basis point, the strategy's own commission: charge one horse and not the other and the
> unfunded one wins. With the control paying its own way, gross selection alpha at the daily
> clock is **+0.67%/yr, not −0.69%/yr**. The verdict is unchanged — *t* = +0.35 is still
> nothing — but the reason it was reached was an artefact. A one-sided cost ledger is the most
> common way a backtest lies in the direction of its author's thesis, and a sceptical thesis
> is not exempt.

## Synthetic control (machinery proof — never supports the stamp)

- **Planted panel** (persistent, slowly-decaying expected returns): gross Sharpe **5.78 /
  5.53 / 4.87 / 3.44** for daily / weekly / monthly / quarterly (HAC *t* = 17.7 / 16.9 /
  15.0 / 10.6), and the daily arm earns **+13.9 pp/yr more gross** than the quarterly one.
  The harness recovers exactly the mechanism a turnover budget prices — a faster clock
  tracks a decaying signal better — when that mechanism is present.
- **Null panel** (market factor + idiosyncratic noise only): gross Sharpe −0.030 / −0.135 /
  −0.154 / +0.025, every |*t*| ≤ 0.67. Across 6 seeds the monthly gross Sharpe has mean
  **−0.048**, sd 0.232, largest magnitude 0.405. The detector is unbiased.

The real-tape flatness is therefore a property of **sector momentum**, not of the engine.

## Verdict

- **Signal — None.** The sleeve has no gross edge to budget at any speed: the best gross
  HAC *t* over 26.5 years is **+0.67**, every bootstrap Sharpe CI straddles zero, and no
  speed-vs-speed race clears |*t*| = 2. The quarterly arm is +0.013. The parameter
  neighbourhood tops out at *t* = +0.55, so the published setting is neither lucky nor
  load-bearing. The one arm that *looks* significant — long-only, *t* ≈ +2.6 against cash —
  is beta: against a cost-matched, same-clock equal-weight control its selection alpha is
  +0.67% to −0.31%/yr gross with every |*t*| ≤ 0.35.
  Survivorship is minimal by construction (all eleven SPDRs still trade) but not zero:
  XLRE and XLC are in the panel because the GICS committee carved them out, a decision
  taken with hindsight the 1999 investor did not have. The engine also reads a missing
  daily return as zero, which is harmless on a panel with no delistings and would not be
  on one that has them.
- **Tradability — Mirage.** The honest budget is **2.5 bps at daily, 4.8 weekly, 10.1
  monthly and negative at quarterly**, and it is a budget for a return that is
  statistically zero. At a realistic 5 bps and 40 bps borrow, three of four speeds are
  net-negative and the fourth (monthly, +0.037) is indistinguishable from cash. The
  ranking of speeds inverts **below 1 bp**, so the "which frequency is best"
  question is decided entirely by an execution assumption rather than by the tape. And
  the era cut swaps the winner. There is nothing here to size.
- **What the study does establish.** The turnover ladder itself is solid arithmetic and
  transfers to any sleeve: a daily clock on an 11-name cross-section trades **31× NAV a
  year**, ~92% of it genuine rank churn, and therefore needs ~5× the gross edge of a
  monthly clock to break even. Read the break-even column as the price of admission, and
  ask of any signal whether its *gross* alpha clears it — this one does not.
